source: Edition facts copied from the EES-OPEN-N research (OSS-CANDIDATES.md section F), which quotes Microsoft Learn. Nothing here is from memory. Where the source says UNKNOWN or contested the label is kept and NOT decided.

proStatusValues.NOT-AVAILABLE: Microsoft Learn states the feature is not available on Windows Pro. A failing finding becomes NOT-APPLICABLE-EDITION on a Pro target.
proStatusValues.CONTESTED: Microsoft Learn contradicts itself. Label kept as CONTESTED; the outcome is NOT changed.
proStatusValues.UNKNOWN: Not established. Label kept as UNKNOWN; the outcome is NOT changed.
proStatusValues.AVAILABLE: Microsoft Learn states the feature is available on Windows Pro.

rules.note: Learn: Pro = No, Enterprise = Yes, Education = Yes; entitled by Windows Enterprise E3/E5 and Education A3/A5, not Pro. Learn also notes Pro devices that previously ran it can retain it (known-issues page): a PASSING finding is therefore never relabelled.
Learn edition table: Personal Data Encryption = No for Windows Pro.
Learn edition table: Zero Trust DNS = No for Windows Pro.
Learn edition table: Always On VPN device tunnel = No for Windows Pro.

Learn contradicts itself. The edition tab and the AppLocker CSP page say Pro is supported; the licensing tab says No for Windows Pro (Yes for Enterprise E3); the Enterprise E3 in CSP page lists AppLocker management as not found in Windows Pro; the feature-availability page says AppLocker policies are supported on all editions of Windows 10 2004+ with KB5024351 and via MDM on all editions. Kept as CONTESTED. Not decided here.
